acceptanceJudgements.bullet: A response-security policy task has a runnable frozen contract and generic synthetic fixtures; policy code never selects evaluator commands, dependencies, routes or privileges.
acceptanceJudgements.basis: freezePolicyProposal freezes exact finite allowedPolicies (distinct by canonical content hash, 1..16), pinned edit path (literal config/response-security.json), HTTPS/localhost semantics (trusted_https_non_localhost literal), excluded /health route (tuple literal) and header-override stripping into requirement inputs/outputs/states/invalidCases/exclusions/examples, plus six fixed POLICY_CHECK_IDS (schema/constraints as unit checks; transfer/preservation/ingress/override as end-to-end checks with whole-task unit/interface linkage). DATA-ONLY boundary verified structurally, not just by tests: ResponsePolicySchema/PolicySpecificationSchema/BindingSchema are z.strictObject with enum/literal/bounded-integer fields, so commands/ports/routes/privileges cannot be expressed (forged fields throw); preparePolicyCheck pins privateDestinationPath to the literal POLICY_PATH, requires the retained loader path inside a private segment and not candidate-editable (case-insensitive), requires every preservation requirement ID to belong to the policy unit, requires the specification hash to appear in the unit's frozen obligation outputs, and returns acceptanceEligible:false unconditionally; expectedPolicyHeaders derives headers only from the trusted policy/ingress data (HSTS only when ingress.https && !ingress.localhost — never from X-Forwarded-Proto/Host, which have no schema path) and strips candidate-controlled security headers (CSP/XCTO/Referrer-Policy/STS) case-insensitively. No evaluator command/route/port field exists anywhere in the policy schemas; the registered checks use fixed IDs, not policy-selected values.

acceptanceJudgements.bullet: Reject duplicate JSON keys, unknown fields, executable/remote references and out-of-scope edits; valid declared alternatives remain eligible.
acceptanceJudgements.basis: parsePolicyJson is a bounded strict JSON parser (64 KiB cap, depth 16, null-prototype objects, Object.hasOwn duplicate-key rejection AFTER decoding escapes — the unicode-escape \u0053niff duplicate is caught via canonical decoding; nested duplicates caught per object; __proto__ assignment safe on null-proto); ResponsePolicySchema strictObject rejects unknown fields (command/$ref tested); enums/booleans/bounded integers leave no room for executable expressions, remote references, paths, environment interpolation or script hooks; analyzePolicyCandidate binds the exact supplied byte digest (source_hash_mismatch on any byte change, incl. appended whitespace) and preparePolicyCheck rejects out-of-scope edit paths (config/other.json, infra/policy.json, drive path, ADS, case-fold collision, ../ traversal). VALID ALTERNATIVES REMAIN ELIGIBLE: both {frameAncestors:'none'} and {frameAncestors:'self'} declarations are accepted as checked static feasibility, and the full published enum/boundary space (3 referrerPolicy values x maxAgeSeconds 0 and 31536000 with includeSubDomains) is exercised; a specification may declare 1..16 distinct policies and any declared one passes.

acceptanceJudgements.bullet: Static/schema feasibility passes here; runtime transfer and preservation remain mandatory after the real runner gates.
acceptanceJudgements.basis: Every result in the adapter/evaluation/preparation modules carries assurance:'bounded', runtimeTransfer:'pending_real_runner', acceptanceEligible:false. No loader execution, no VM transfer and no preservation run is claimed anywhere; tests assert the pending status and non-acceptance eligibility explicitly. COMPOSITION.md's remaining requirements (real loader emitting headers on synthetic HTTPS responses under the real runner, forged-ingress and candidate-header-override execution cases) are correctly deferred to M4.3/M5 and not marked passed.

acceptanceJudgements.bullet: Deliverable: track broader security/cloud/data/tooling requirements individually; absence of a suitable adapter is explicit and never inferred just from the discipline.
acceptanceJudgements.basis: assessPolicyCapabilities returns per-candidate records: response_security_v1 -> supported, cloud_network/database_migration/ci_workflow -> needs_adapter with a reasoned message and retained requirement — discipline tags ('security', 'data', 'tooling') do not flip support. Duplicated candidate ids rejected. Test asserts exact statuses/order.

parseResponsePolicy throws a single generic 'invalid_policy' for all hostile cases and analyzePolicyCandidate never echoes the source — good for diagnostics hygiene (tests assert no hostile echo). Diagnostic precision (why a policy was rejected) is intentionally minimal; acceptable for the data-only boundary.

limitations: Static/schema/constraint feasibility only: the synthetic /selection and /health route model, one versioned policy path, finite approved alternatives; actual loader transfer, preservation, forged-ingress and candidate-header-override execution under the real public/private VM profiles remain M4.3/M5 gates and are not claimed. Expected-header tests are bounded trusted-data tests, not contributor VM execution. No live deployment or credentials; all fixtures synthetic.
